IDEAEvent.EventNarrative: Parent provided written consent for initial evaluation of student.
Team determined student eligibility for special education services.
Parent declined consent for IEP implementation at this time.
Special education services initiated as outlined in the IEP.
Behavioral incident documented requiring formal review.
Student placement moved to more restrictive environment per team decision.
Manifestation determination review conducted for disciplinary action.
Formal parent complaint filed regarding services or placement.
Student identified as potentially requiring surrogate parent.
Qualified surrogate parent assigned to represent student interests.
Due process hearing officer officially assigned to case.
Formal due process hearing conducted with all parties present.
Written decision issued by SEA/LEA following hearing proceedings.
Corrective action taken in response to compliance finding.
Annual IEP review date is upcoming and requires scheduling.
Annual IEP review meeting completed and IEP updated accordingly.
Transfer student records and evaluation report completed.
Transfer student IEP adopted pending new IEP development.
Parent submitted written withdrawal of consent for IEP services.
IEP development process finalized and document completed.
Secondary manifestation determination review completed by team.
Initial evaluation referral received and timeline initiated.
Re-evaluation completed per three-year timeline requirements.
Extended school year eligibility determination completed.
Secondary transition plan reviewed and updated for student.

StudentIEPGoal.IEPGoalDetails: Student will demonstrate grade-level reading comprehension skills by correctly answering inferential and literal questions with 80% accuracy across 4 consecutive sessions.
Student will independently complete daily living tasks including self-care routines with no more than one verbal prompt across 3 consecutive observation periods.
Student will identify and apply post-secondary education and employment options aligned with personal strengths and interests in 4 out of 5 structured planning activities.
Student will demonstrate proficiency in core academic content standards through participation in transition coursework with 75% mastery on assessments.
Student will use self-regulation strategies to manage academic frustration and remain on task for at least 20 consecutive minutes in 4 out of 5 observed sessions.
Student will accurately perform multi-step math problem solving involving real-world applications with 80% accuracy over 3 consecutive probes.
Student will demonstrate functional communication skills by initiating and responding to peer interactions using augmentative or verbal means in 4 out of 5 opportunities.
Student will apply organizational and study skills strategies to independently complete long-term assignments with minimal teacher prompting across 4 sessions.
Student will increase written expression skills by composing structured paragraphs with a topic sentence, supporting details, and a conclusion with 75% accuracy.
Student will demonstrate progress in social-emotional learning by identifying emotions and applying coping strategies in 4 out of 5 structured opportunities.
Student will participate in community-based instruction activities that support post-secondary independent living goals with 80% task completion.
Student will demonstrate functional academic skills in reading and math within real-world contexts at a level commensurate with post-secondary transition goals.
Student will independently navigate campus and community environments using orientation and mobility strategies with no more than 2 prompts per session.
Student will demonstrate improvement in fine motor skills necessary for academic tasks by completing timed activities with increasing speed and accuracy.
Student will apply behavior intervention strategies to reduce targeted interfering behaviors to fewer than 2 occurrences per 30-minute observation period.
Student will demonstrate comprehension of grade-aligned science and social studies content through modified assessments with 70% accuracy.
Student will develop and articulate a post-secondary vision statement identifying at least two goals each for education, employment, and independent living.
Student will use assistive technology tools to access grade-level curriculum and demonstrate content mastery on 3 consecutive assessments.
Student will increase oral reading fluency to an age-appropriate rate by reading connected text at a target rate with no more than 5 errors per 100 words.
Student will independently manage a daily schedule including transitions between activities with no more than one adult prompt across 4 observations.
Student will demonstrate functional use of money and time management skills in simulated and community settings with 80% accuracy.
Student will exhibit appropriate peer and adult interaction behaviors by initiating conversations and taking turns with 80% success in structured settings.
Student will apply phonics and word recognition strategies to decode multi-syllabic words with 75% accuracy on curriculum-based assessments.
Student will demonstrate knowledge of post-secondary options by creating a transition portfolio including career exploration and self-advocacy documentation.
Student will improve handwriting legibility and written output rate to meet classroom participation expectations across 4 consecutive samples.
Student will correctly apply mathematical reasoning to problem-solving tasks involving fractions, decimals, and percentages with 80% accuracy.
Student will develop self-advocacy skills by identifying personal learning needs and communicating accommodations to teachers in 3 out of 4 opportunities.
